Figure 1:Compositional interaction requires grounded decisions.Top: Trajectory2Gym constructs linked interactions (1) and checks each training
action against that history (2). Bottom: a Tau2 Retail user requests a
larger bottle and a dimmer lamp, then confirms only the lamp. Both rules
judge the same two candidate actions. Filtering by execution keeps both
because native tool replay accepts both requests. Trajectory2Gym uses catalog
evidence and the latest confirmation to keep the lamp exchange and reject
the additional bottle exchange. Green checks mark correct selection
decisions; the red cross marks erroneous retention. This schematic illustrates supervision
selection with paraphrased dialogue and a constructed second candidate.

Figure 5:Grounded supervision within a compositional interaction.A failed email lookup remains visible context without receiving imitation
loss. Subsequent visible evidence supports identity recovery, cancellation,
address modification, and catalog-grounded item updates.
Dialogue and tool fields are abridged for display.

Figure 6:Changing intent during a stateful interaction.Simia submits an exchange before a later return request, which the changed
order state prevents. In the independently generated Trajectory2Gym dialogue,
the user changes the request before submission and the return succeeds.
The different histories make this a behavior illustration, not an
identical-context comparison.

Figure 7:Delegating phone-side actions and using feedback.MUA-RL repeatedly attempts phone-side operations unavailable to the
assistant. Trajectory2Gym delegates those operations to the user and adapts
its continuation to the reported device state and connection speed,
completing the task.

Figure 8:Recovery enables dependent operations.After a route error, Simia proposes a lookup but does not complete the
booking. Trajectory2Gym retrieves the needed airport codes, books the flight,
and reuses the returned booking identifier for invoice and support calls.
Only the Trajectory2Gym interaction satisfies the native task checker.

Figure 9:An early return blocks later exchange attempts.LoopTool submits a return before confirmation, leaving later exchange
and cancellation attempts invalid. Trajectory2Gym preserves the delivered
state while obtaining confirmation, then submits the user-selected
exchange.

Figure 10:A correct fare does not complete the workflow.Both agents report the correct fare, but Simia does not execute the
requested booking. Trajectory2Gym books the flight and uses its returned
identifier for the subsequent insurance operation, completing the
dependent workflow.

Figure 11:Remaining failure against a successful external baseline.Simia completes payment, line resumption, and device repair.
Trajectory2Gym transfers after sending a payment request, leaving the
connectivity and overdue-bill checks unsatisfied.
This case retains an external-agent success and a Trajectory2Gym failure.
